transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess my family thought I’d gotten a little carried away with a project at the house. I was buying wood, lights, display things… maybe more than I should’ve, from our savings. I just felt like it was important to keep going, even after dark. Like if I stopped, the house—and maybe the whole block—would miss its chance. I know that probably sounds odd, but I was trying to make something good, you know?
During this time, were you needing much less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, I probably wasn’t keeping the best hours, but I didn’t really think of it as “needing less sleep.” I was just… busy with what I was doing, you know? Is that the kind of thing you mean?
At the time, did you believe you had a special power or mission connected to what you were building?

Well… I wouldn’t want to say “special power,” exactly. That sounds a little much, doesn’t it? But at the time, yes, I did feel like I understood what that old Schiller Park house could become in a way other people just didn’t. Like with the lights and the pictures, I could make it into something important—something people would come see. I really believed that.
During that time, did you hear or see things that other people could not?

I don’t… I don’t think so. Not like seeing things that weren’t there, or hearing voices, if that’s what you mean. I was very focused on what I was doing, and maybe I read more into things than I should have, but I can’t say I noticed anything like that. Is that okay to say?
At that time, were you feeling unusually high, euphoric, or especially irritable?

I guess… yes, in a way. I felt pretty charged up most days, almost joyful, like I was young again and had all this purpose. I don’t want to make it sound like I was out of control, but if my wife or the contractors questioned what I was doing, I could get hot fast… I’d start yelling. I’m not proud of that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d call it that, doctor. I’ve had down days, of course… times where I felt low or discouraged. But a full two weeks where I was depressed most of the day nearly every day—I don’t know. I can’t honestly say I remember it that clearly. Is that okay?
Did that belief about the house being especially important continue even after your mood and energy returned to normal?

I think… no, not really. Before I got all charged up with the remodeling and making the house into something important, I wasn’t noticing special meaning in things like trucks going by or how the neighbors looked at me. That sort of thing only started once I felt driven about the house project. I don’t think it kept going the same way after I settled down. Is that what you’re asking?
Before this house project, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt unusually energized or driven like this?

I’m not sure, doctor. I mean, I’ve had times in life where I got interested in something or worked hard, sure… but like this house project, with that kind of push behind it? I don’t know that I can point to another time like that. I’d hate to say yes if I’m not remembering it right.
At any point in your life, have you ever gone through a time when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day, for at least two weeks?

I don’t think so, doctor. I mean, I’ve had sad spells and rough days like anybody, but I can’t really say there was a stretch of two whole weeks where I was depressed nearly all day, every day. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just to be agreeable.
Before this house project, was there ever another time in your life when you felt unusually energetic or driven in a similar way?

Well… before the house, I don’t think it was quite the same. But lately, yes, I mean—I can’t seem to just sit in the chair like I used to. I’m up and moving around, going from the garden to the darkroom to the porch, carrying tools, fixing little things before anybody even asks me to. I tell myself I’m just being useful, you know… but I suppose that’s the kind of driven you mean?
Before the house project, was there ever another distinct period when you felt unusually energized or driven like this?

I know I’ve kind of said this already, doctor, but… no, before the house project I can’t really think of a separate spell like that. What I do notice is this recent thing where I can’t just sit in my chair anymore. I’m up going from the garden to the darkroom to the porch, carrying tools around, fixing little things before anybody even asks. I tell myself I’m just keeping busy, but… maybe that’s what you’re asking about.
Aside from the house project, has there ever been another separate time in your life when you felt unusually energetic or driven in a similar way?

I’m sorry, I know I may be going over the same thing… but no, not really another separate time that I can point to. It’s more this recent stretch where I can’t seem to just sit in my chair anymore. I’m up and down, out to the garden, then the darkroom, then the porch, carrying tools around and fixing things before anyone even asks me to. I tell myself I’m just trying to be helpful, but maybe that’s what you mean by driven.
Has there been a separate time, distinct from the house project, when you felt unusually energized or driven like this?

I don’t think there was some other separate time, no… not that I can point to. It’s really been this lately, where I just can’t seem to stay in the chair. I keep getting up, going out to the garden, then over to the darkroom, then the porch—carrying tools around, fixing little things before anybody even asks me to. I tell myself I’m just helping, you know… that’s all right to say, isn’t it?
Has this recent stretch of being unable to sit still been a separate episode from the house project, with a time in between when you felt back to your usual self?

No… I don’t think there was really a break in between where I felt back to normal. It’s been sort of one long stretch, I guess. About three months now, since the remodeling started and the whole house got turned upside down. I mean, I’ve tried to make it sound like I’m just helping out, but it’s been going on that whole time, if that answers it right.
